name: David Hume
worldviewSummary: Hume is an empiricist and skeptic: our beliefs about causes rest on custom and habit rather than reason, morality springs from sentiment rather than reason, and one cannot derive what ought to be from what is. A wise person proportions belief to the evidence.
biography: Scottish philosopher, historian and essayist. His Treatise of Human Nature (1739–40) was poorly received at first; he later recast it in the Enquiries. He also wrote a widely read History of England.

works.title: An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals

concepts.description: Authors often move from statements about what is to statements about what ought to be without explaining how this new relation can be deduced.
Inferences from past to future experience presuppose that nature is uniform, which cannot itself be proven by reason without circularity; custom, not reason, is the guide of life.

concepts.concept: Reason as slave of the passions
concepts.description: Reason alone cannot motivate action; it serves the passions by informing them about means and matters of fact.

positions.statement: A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence; testimony to miracles can never outweigh the uniform experience that establishes laws of nature.
Moral distinctions derive from a moral sense or sentiment of approval and disapproval, notably sympathy and the perception of what is useful or agreeable.
We never observe a necessary connection between cause and effect, only constant conjunction; the idea of necessity comes from the mind's habitual expectation.
When we introspect we find only a bundle of perceptions in perpetual flux, never a simple, enduring self.
